rounds.q: In 1900, what % of the world's kids died before age 5?
rounds.why: By 2024 it was under 4%, roughly 1 child in 27.
rounds.src: Our World in Data, Child mortality (Gapminder & UN IGME)
rounds.fun: From 41% in 1900 to under 4% by 2024. So many more kids got to blow out 5 candles!

rounds.q: In 1900, how long did the average person on Earth live?
rounds.why: Child deaths pulled the average down. By 2023 it was about 73 years.
rounds.src: Our World in Data, Life expectancy (Riley; UN WPP)
rounds.fun: A 1900 newborn could expect about 32 years. By 2023, about 73. Way more time to play!

rounds.q: In 1900, what % of the world's adults could read and write?
rounds.why: By 2024 the global literacy rate was about 88%.
rounds.src: Our World in Data, Literacy rate (historical estimates + UNESCO)
rounds.fun: In 1900 only about 1 in 5 adults could read. Now it's about 88%. Books for everyone!

rounds.q: In 1900, what % of the world's people lived in cities?
rounds.src: Our World in Data, urban population share (HYDE; UN WUP)
rounds.fun: Back in 1900, only 16% lived in towns and cities. Most folks were country folks!

rounds.q: About how many cars were on US roads in 1900?
rounds.why: Registration wasn't even required yet. New York was the first state to ask for it, in 1901.
rounds.fun: About 8,000 cars for the whole country. Traffic jams were basically a rumor!
